label: TSMM to TRQP binding
description: Maps TRQP stack concepts into TSMM abstractions so TSMM can act as the semantic layer across assurance, conformance, and trusted service provider publication flows.

mappings.description: Authority defining operating rules, publication criteria, and acceptable evidence.
The published ecosystem participant whose assertions and status are evaluated.
conditions: May be modeled as Agent where service acts autonomously.

mappings.description: Evidence submitted to substantiate conformance or operational trust posture.
Profile determining required controls and evidence depth.
Actor depending on registry-mediated trust decisions downstream.

notes: TRQP publication flows can be expressed as TSMM graph instances and surfaced through the TSMM registry format.
This binding is intentionally semantic rather than normative and does not override TRQP wording.

guarantees.name: authority-resolution
guarantees.description: TRQP governance and publication roles can be modeled through TSMM authority and registry abstractions.

guarantees.name: evidence-portability
guarantees.description: Conformance and assurance evidence can travel as TSMM evidence-bearing objects.

guarantees.name: revocation-propagation
guarantees.description: Revocation can be represented, but ecosystem-specific propagation timing remains outside TSMM.

limitations.name: protocol-specific query semantics
limitations.impact: TSMM does not reproduce TRQP transport or query behavior.
limitations.mitigation: Use TRQP-specific protocol documentation alongside the binding.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Published trust objects retain authority source, evidence references, and status context.
Downstream consumers treat TSMM trust decisions as context-bound and evidence-backed rather than as timeless endorsements.

notes: Validation vector exercises binding maturity coverage without asserting full production readiness.
